Item 1. Business Description

Berkshire Hathaway Inc. is a holding company owning subsidiaries engaged in a number of diverse business activities, including insurance and reinsurance, freight rail transportation, utilities and energy, manufacturing, retailing and services, with each subsidiary operating with a high degree of autonomy under its own management team and reporting periodically to headquarters on capital allocation and operating performance across its respective industry. Our insurance subsidiaries underwrite a broad range of property, casualty and life products, while our non-insurance subsidiaries span rail transportation, utilities and energy generation, industrial manufacturing, and a wide variety of retailing and service businesses acquired over many decades.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Berkshire and its subsidiaries are subject to extensive regulation across the insurance, utilities, energy and rail industries in which they operate, and changes in that regulatory environment, along with catastrophe losses in our insurance operations, could materially affect our consolidated results of operations in any given period. We are also exposed to significant fluctuations in the market value of our equity investment portfolio, which can produce large swings in reported net earnings from one period to the next without reflecting any change in the underlying economic performance of our operating businesses.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis

Net earnings attributable to Berkshire shareholders varied significantly between periods, substantially due to unrealized gains and losses on our equity investment portfolio, which we believe are not indicative of the underlying performance of our operating businesses taken as a whole across the reporting period. Operating earnings across our insurance and non-insurance subsidiaries were broadly consistent with the prior year, reflecting the diversified nature of our subsidiary base and the long operating histories of most of our largest businesses.
